To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Latin American energy supply investments will need to double between 2010-2050 to meet the projected energy demand. Climate control policies will increase this investment need by 45%.

(i) the business as usual investment scenario is characterized by high growth in absolute terms, but declining as share of GDP; (ii) climate control measures lead to a doubling in annual investment in electricity supply in 2050, as well as a doubling in cumulative investment; and (iii) the required investment is mainly directed towards low carbon electricity generation technologies and CCS.
Latin America's energy sector needs to invest 2 trillion USD in energy supply between 2010-2050, of which 1.4 tril USD is for electricity generation.

the question how to achieve a sustainable energy system in Latin America. Our analysis suggests, that the region is on the right track in terms of energy policy, but that additional efforts are required to achieve the ambitious climate targets.

the Latin American energy sector will require substantial investments over the coming decades, regardless of the climate policy scenario.
